title: Water pump weep hole leak (colored drip under the engine)

beats.visual: A few bright colored coolant drops beading on grey concrete beneath a dark engine bay, oil-stained garage floor, macro, no people
beats.narration: A few colored drops underneath, not always the radiator.

beats.visual: A water pump housing on a steel bench, cast aluminum body and pulley, a tiny weep hole in the casting catching the light, macro
beats.narration: Water pumps have a weep hole that seeps first.

beats.visual: A single bead of coolant swelling at that weep hole and running down the cast housing, raking light, shallow focus, no hands
beats.narration: That seep is the early warning.

beats.visual: Two drops side by side on concrete, one bright and syrupy, one clear and thin, hard light, extreme macro
beats.narration: Colored and sticky, not clear like condensation.

beats.visual: A dried crusty coolant trail crusted down the pump housing and across the belt edge, chalky pale texture, close macro, dim shop light
beats.narration: A dried crusty trail shows before any puddle.

igfbCopy.primaryCaption: A few drops of colored fluid under the front of your engine isn't always "just the radiator." Water pumps are built with a tiny weep hole that leaks a little before the seal fails for good. Catch it early and it's a simple fix — ignore it and it can mean overheating on the road. Stop by and we'll take a look.

adVariants.hook: That small puddle under your car might be a built-in warning.
adVariants.caption: Water pumps have a weep hole on purpose — it drips a little before the seal fails completely. Catching it now beats a tow later.
adVariants.cta: Stop by and we'll take a look — no guessing.

adVariants.hook: Colored drops under the engine, not under the AC?
adVariants.caption: That's coolant, not condensation — and it's often the first sign a water pump seal is wearing out. One clue: it's sticky, not clear.
adVariants.cta: Worth a quick look — swing by.
